ios.desc:
YOUR FEEDS. NOW ON AIR.

Choose the sources you care about and press Play. Robot Radio turns followed feeds into a continuous lineup of short, presenter-led reports. Browse curated stations across news, technology, science, culture, and more, or build My Station around your own feeds.

A program to turn on, not another reading queue. Discover a story, open the original, or stay for the next report.

WATCH YOUR KINDLE LIBRARY

Sign into you Kindle account and read aloud your favorites with an animated presenter. (NOTE: Kindle page layout must be set to SINGLE COLUMN, or it will not sound right).

START WITH SIRI

Copy a link, an article passage, or a long AI response from another app. Then say:
“Hey Siri, Crunch broadcast.”

Import your source, create an outline, and watch an animated explanation with your current settings.
“Hey Siri, Crunch audiobook.”

Hear the full text, not a summary. Playback starts when narration is ready.

Nothing to copy? Say “Hey Siri, Crunch radio” to open Robot Radio, then choose a station and press Play. More Siri and Shortcuts actions open sources, start research, tune stations, and return to your last audiobook.

HEAR THE WHOLE STORY

Audiobook Mode reads the full text of articles, documents, and EPUBs with expressive on-device narration. Return to your saved place or move between sections. Your own reading becomes your listening library.

GO DEEPER. DIRECT THE EXPLANATION.

Ask questions about a source and follow available citations back to supporting passages. Explore Executive, Technical, and Study Guide modes, or use Focus Mode to investigate a particular question across the source.

Shape a briefing, study explanation, or product introduction through conversation. Change the tone, length, audience, or focus. Choose a response or transcript and press Broadcast.

KEEP THE VIDEO

Replay, save, or share your presenter-led segment with available source imagery. Keep a briefing, revisit an explanation, or share what you learned. Generation waits stay out of the finished video.

BRING YOUR SOURCES

Import articles, PDFs, EPUBs, text, feeds, and research papers. Find more with Discover Assistant and save sources for offline reading.

Supported sources include RSS, Atom, Medium, Substack, Ghost, WordPress, Wikipedia, arXiv, DOI, PubMed, LaTeX, Reddit, YouTube, and Vimeo. Available text, imagery, and transcripts vary by source.

ON-DEVICE AI. ONE PURCHASE.

Apple Intelligence powers summaries and research. Qwen generates speech loc
